![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14228735/assets/9ce1b06ac9fc3caeed0a1f7866511be42b4c127a0bdddfd40b74e211ed24e02a.png)

Find the global extrema of the function $f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}$ on the closed region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4\},$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x,y)$ is continuous on the closed, bounded region $D,$ the function attains a global maximum and minimum on $D.$

To find the extreme values, we follow three steps.

**Step 1.** Find the critical points of $f$ inside the region. 

To determine the critical points, we solve ${f}^{′}=0.$ Computing the derivative gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2},\,4xy\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative exists at each point inside $D,$ and it equals zero when

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}=0 \\ 4xy=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x=R \\ y=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the entire segment of solutions $\{(x,0)\,:\,x\in [0,2]\}.$ Since all these points do not belong to the interior of $D,$ we do not yet include them in the list of candidates for extrema (they lie on the boundary of $D,$ so we will consider them in the next step).

**Step 2.**  Find the points on the boundary of $D$ that could give rise to extreme values. 

To find the points on the boundary that could give rise to extreme values, we parametrize each part of the boundary:

- The line connecting $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨t,0⟩,\,t\in (0,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,0) \\  & =2(t)(0)^{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $F(t)$ is constant. So, $F(t)$ does not have local extremum points on the open interval $t\in (0,2).$

- The line connecting $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨0,t⟩,\,t\in (0,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on this boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(0,t) \\  & =2(0)(t)^{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $F(t)$ is constant. So, $F(t)$ does not have local extremum points on the open interval $t\in (0,2).$

- The quarter-circle connecting $(0,2)$ and $(2,0)$ can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨t,\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}⟩,\,t\in (0,2).\end{aligned}
$$

The values of $f$ on the boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}) \\  & =2(t)(\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}})^{2} \\  & =8t-2{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (0,2),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ (8t-2{t}^{3})^{′} & =0 \\ 8-6{t}^{2} & =0 \\ 2(4-3{t}^{2}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation gives one solution, $t=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3},$ inside the interval $t\in (0,2).$
Evaluating the corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ on the boundary, we obtain one  candidate point, $(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3},\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}).$

Also, we have to include the corner points of the region as candidates for extrema. So, in total we obtain four candidates:

$$
(0,0),\,(2,0),\,(0,2),\,(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3},\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3})
$$

**Step 3.** Evaluate $f(x,y)$ at each of the candidate points, and compare their values. 

Evaluating $f(x,y)$ at each of the points mentioned above, we get the following: 

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,0)$ | $(2,0)$ | $(0,2)$ | $(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3},\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3})$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\frac{32\sqrt{3}}{9}$ |

Therefore, on the closed region $D,$ we have that 

- $f$ attains the global minimum of $0$ at the points on the line segment connecting $(0,0)$ and $(2,0),$ and on the line segment connecting $(0,0)$ and $(0,2),$ and

- $f$ attains the global maximum of $\frac{32\sqrt{3}}{9}$ at the point $(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3},\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}).$
